one_liner: Set up, pin, debug, and profile the CUDA/PyTorch/HF/DeepSpeed/vLLM stack for real LLM work.

key_terms.definition: The rule that a GPU driver supports CUDA runtimes only up to a max version; PyTorch bundles its own CUDA but flash-attn/bitsandbytes compile against the system CUDA toolkit.
The backend used for multi-GPU/multi-node collective operations (all-reduce, etc.); its timeouts and debug logs are the primary diagnostic for distributed hangs and network failures.
PyTorch API that JIT-compiles a model's forward pass via TorchInductor, giving 20-40% speedups; modes 'reduce-overhead' (inference) and 'max-autotune' (training) trade compile time for runtime speed.
A multi-GPU abstraction library that auto-detects the environment and wraps training code for DDP, FSDP, or DeepSpeed with a single `accelerate launch` entry point and config file.
DeepSpeed's memory-sharding scheme with stages that progressively shard optimizer states (stage 1), gradients (stage 2), and model parameters (stage 3) across GPUs, optionally offloading to CPU.
A pip package implementing FlashAttention's tiled, IO-aware attention kernel that avoids materializing the full N×N attention matrix; must be installed with --no-build-isolation after torch.
A library enabling 8-bit optimizers (e.g., Adam8bit) and 4-bit weight quantization (NF4/INT4) for fine-tuning and inference on memory-constrained GPUs.
A high-throughput LLM inference server built on PagedAttention that exposes an OpenAI-compatible API and supports tensor parallelism and prefix caching.
An inference server and structured-generation framework built on RadixAttention (prefix caching via a radix tree), supporting constrained/schema-based generation.
HuggingFace's library providing trainers (SFTTrainer, GRPOTrainer, etc.) for supervised fine-tuning and RL-based post-training of language models.
An experiment-tracking tool for logging training metrics, qualitative sample tables, and versioned artifacts (datasets, checkpoints) tied to each run.

A memory-saving technique (enabled via `model.gradient_checkpointing_enable()`) that recomputes activations during backward pass instead of storing them, reducing GPU memory at the cost of extra compute.

prerequisites: the attention mechanism and KV cache
